newsitem.title: USA: Fugitive drug suspect arrested, returned to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive drug suspect arrested, returned to U.S.

text.p: A drug suspect who escaped from a Georgia jail more than three years ago was arrested in Colombia and returned to the United States on Wednesday to face trial on cocaine charges, the U.S. Marshals Service said.

Oscar Albert Torres, 53, was awaiting trial and a possible life sentence for possession and intent to distribute 50 kilograms of cocaine when he escaped from prison in Moultrie, Ga., with outside assistance by cutting through cell bars and security fences with a torch.

Torres, a native of Cuba, was one of the Marshals Service's "15 Most Wanted" fugitives and had a criminal history dating back to 1962, including a five-year sentence in 1973 for the sale of narcotics, agency director Eduardo Gonzalez said in a written statement.

Torres was arrested by Colombian authorities in Barranquilla earlier this week as a result of investigative efforts by officers of the Colombian National Police, the Marshals Service, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, Gonzalez said.
Following his arrest, Torres was flown to Miami aboard a commercial aircraft and held in custody there pending his transfer to Georgia.

"We considered Torres a dangerous fugitive and placed a high priority on his arrest," Gonzalez said. "His apprehension reflects not only on the excellent international cooperation that took place between law enforcement agencies, but also the strong determination of the investigators involved to locate this fugitive from justice."
